newsitem.title: USA: California memorial service held for Andrew Cunanan.
newsitem.headline: California memorial service held for Andrew Cunanan.

text.p: The family and godparents of suspected spree serial killer Andrew Cunanan, who committed suicide last week, quietly said goodbye to him at a private memorial service, a church spokeswoman said on Wednesday.

The service, attended by only a handful of people, was held on Monday night at St. Rita's Church in suburban National City, a church secretary told Reuters. Church officials had declined comment on Tuesday.
"Yes, the service was held here at St. Rita's," the secretary said. She declined to elaborate on the proceedings and the church pastor, Father Jovencio Ricafort, was unavailable for comment.

Cunanan, who was wanted for five murders in four states committed during a coast-to-coast killing spree that started in April, shot himself to death in Miami Beach last week, eight days after allegedly killing his final victim, renowned Italian fashion designer Gianni Versace.
Delfin Labao, Cunanan's godfather and a close family friend, told the San Diego Union-Tribune newspaper that the service was "very reverend, very consoling."
During the service, attended by Cunanan's mother, MaryAnn Cunanan, his siblings and his godparents, Cunanan, 27, was remembered as "our beloved boy," Labao said.
"It was what the family needed, especially in this time of understanding and accepting what Andrew had just done for himself," he added.
Labao told the Union Tribune that a priest delivered Mass during the service and each of the mourners related their happy memories of Cunanan.
Meanwhile, the Federal Bureau of Investigation was analysing DNA and fingerprints taken from Cunanan's body in the hope of unlocking some of the secrets he took with him in death.
Police forces in those states where murders have been attributed to Cunanan will be receiving copies of his fingerprints and DNA typing to compare with evidence found on the victims.

He remains the only suspect in the killings of Jeffrey Trail, a former naval office; David Madson, an ex-lover; Chicago real estate developer Lee Miglin, William Reese, a cemetery caretaker, and Versace.
In addition, San Diego police intend to use Cunanan's DNA and fingerprints to determine if he was involved in three unsolved murders of gay men that took place in the city in the last five years.
